blocks.task_summary: Write down a vector equation for L1 in the form r = a + λb.
method_path: Identify point P(-1,1,-13) as position vector a
Identify direction vector b = (7,1,2)
Write r = a + λb

evidence.basis: r = (-1,1,-13) + λ(7,1,2) A1. Note: The r = must be seen.

blocks.task_summary: Find a vector equation for line L2 in the form s = c + μd, given that L2 passes through points A(2,-4,2) and B(7,-6,1).
method_path: Choose position vector c = (2,-4,2) or (7,-6,1)
Calculate direction vector d = B - A = (5,-2,-1) or A - B
Write s = c + μd

evidence.basis: s = (2,-4,2) + μ(5,-2,-1) OR s = (7,-6,1) + μ(5,-2,-1) (or equivalent) A1A1. Note: The s = must be seen.

blocks.task_summary: Show that L1 and L2 are skew.
method_path: Check if direction vectors are parallel: (5,-2,-1) ≠ k(7,1,2) → not parallel
Set up parametric equations for intersection: (-1+7λ, 1+λ, -13+2λ) = (2+5μ, -4-2μ, 2-μ)
Equate two components and solve for λ, μ
Check third component: does not satisfy → no intersection
Conclude lines are not parallel and do not intersect → skew
accepted_alternatives: Use cross product to show not parallel

evidence.basis: 5/7 ≠ -2/1 ≠ -1/2 so L1, L2 are not parallel R1. equating any two components from each line M1. solve simultaneously M1. λ=-1, μ=-2 OR λ=78/17, μ=99/17 OR λ=35/3, μ=-25/3 A1. check for remaining component, e.g. 3rd component: -13+2(-1) ≠ 2+(-1)(-2) R1. hence lines are not parallel and do not intersect, so are skew. AG

blocks.task_summary: Find PN · AB in terms of m.
method_path: Express ON = (2+5μ, -4-2μ, 2-μ)
Calculate PN = ON - OP = (3+5μ, -5-2μ, 15-μ)
Compute dot product PN · AB = (3+5μ, -5-2μ, 15-μ) · (5, -2, -1)
Simplify to 10 + 30μ

evidence.basis: attempt to calculate PN = ON - OP (M1). PN = (3+5μ, -5-2μ, 15-μ) A1. attempt to calculate PN · AB (M1). = 10 + 30μ A1

blocks.task_summary: Given that N is the point on L2 that lies closest to P, find the coordinates of N.
method_path: Set PN · AB = 0 for closest point
Substitute μ into L2 equation to get N = (1/3, -10/3, 7/3)

evidence.basis: setting and solving 10 + 30μ = 0 (M1). μ = -1/3 A1. so N = (1/3, -10/3, 7/3) A1

blocks.task_summary: Find the equation of the plane containing points O, P and N, giving your answer in the form ax + by + γz = d.
method_path: Consider vectors OP = (-1,1,-13) and ON = (1/3, -10/3, 7/3) or equivalent
Find normal vector n = OP × ON = (-123, -6, 9)
Use point O(0,0,0) to get plane equation -123x - 6y + 9z = 0
accepted_alternatives: Use any scalar multiple of normal vector

evidence.basis: considers the vectors (-1,1,-13) and (1/3,-10/3,7/3) or equivalent (A1). attempt to find cross product (M1). = (-123, -6, 9) A1. equation of plane is -123x - 6y + 9z = 0 (or equivalent) A1
